title: Prosecutors seek to have Terrion Arnold wear a tracking device as he awaits trial
content:
Prosecutors asked a Florida judge to require former Detroit Lions defensive back Terrion Arnold to wear a GPS ankle monitor as he awaits trial on robbery and kidnapping charges.

The request came through a court filing in Hillsborough County, Fla., on Tuesday, a day after Judge Christopher C. Sabella rejected the prosecution’s motion to keep Arnold in jail until trial. Instead, Sabella set Arnold’s bail at $1 million while also denying the prosecution’s attempt to require Arnold to wear an ankle monitor. The decision came after Arnold’s attorney, Harvey Steinberg, argued the mandate would have effectively prevented him from playing in the NFL. The league is stringent about the length of players’ socks, so wearing an ankle bracelet during practices or games wouldn’t work.

But the situation around Arnold’s employment has changed since Monday’s hearing. Hours after Sabella’s decision, the Lions released Arnold, their 2024 first-round pick.

“The State’s position is that the Court denied the State’s request for a GPS monitor, due to the representation that the Defendant would be employed by the NFL, and the Defendant would be monitored by his team and the media,” the State Attorney’s Office wrote in Tuesday morning’s filing.

The filing said that Arnold being cut by Detroit “constitutes a change in circumstances.”

As of Tuesday morning, Arnold remained in custody at Falkenburg Road Jail, according to county records. The six other co-defendants in the case also remain in jail.

Arnold faces four kidnapping charges and four robbery charges stemming from a February incident at an apartment in Tampa, Fla. Authorities said three people were beaten and robbed by armed men because Arnold believed two of them stole from him a few days earlier. Arnold was not in the apartment during the incident, but prosecutor Kevin Riley called Arnold the “general manager” of the scheme during Monday’s court hearing. Arnold’s attorneys have said there’s no evidence tying him to the violence or robbery.

Arnold started 15 games as a Lions rookie, but injuries limited him to eight games last season.

His next court date has not yet been set.
